Request page — setup, screens 1–9

Every frame at 390 pt, the iPhone logical width. Light and dark follow your system setting — switch it to see both.

This is not a screenshot and cannot be: the app is SwiftUI and this is HTML. It is here to review the words, the order, and the control types at true width. Do not trust it about spacing, type or color — that comes from the simulator. Both this file and the app's strings are generated from Shared/RequestPage/Copy.json, so what you mark up is what ships.

2 · What this is

A first-run sheet: three feature rows and the cost, before any work is asked for.

◷

A page where people can ask for a time

◆
You choose the times
A handful of offers, worked out from your calendars.
◆
The server never sees your calendar
It holds the times you offer and the requests that come in. Nothing else.
◆
Nothing lands until you accept
Every request comes to this device, and you answer it here.

Setup is free and stays on this device. Publishing needs an AskWhen.me subscription, free for the first 90 days.

3 · Which calendars count

Two checkboxes per calendar, where the owner already is.

Which calendars
HomeBlock for requestsUse for requests
WorkBlock for requestsUse for requests
Referee assignmentsBlock for requestsUse for requests
US HolidaysBlock for requestsUse for requests

Events on a blocking calendar are never offered, and accepted requests are written to the one calendar you mark. Only busy or free is ever read.

Continue

4 · Your page

The one identifying field, and who titles the event.

Your page
Display nameMatt Baylor
One line about it30 minutes, usually about refereeing or calendars.

Your name is the only thing on the page that identifies you; any label works.

When you accept
Event titleMeeting
LocationOptional — a room, or a link

You title the event and the person’s note goes in it; the location goes into the event and the calendar file they receive.

5 · Your day

Asked as a sentence, not a form. Bounds are product decisions.

Your day

My day starts at 9:00 AM and ends at 5:00 PM
Time zone America/Denver
Keep a gap clear 12:00–1:30 PM
Offer on SMTWTFS

Times are in the zone you state, wherever this device travels. The next screen shows what this offers on real dates.

How far ahead14 days
Most requests a day4

Both are privacy controls: a shorter horizon and a lower cap show less of your week’s shape.

Notice I need12 hours

Nothing inside this window is offered, so a request never lands with less warning than this device needs.

How long an offer is30 min
Start times land on:00 and :30
Keep clear either side15 min

Each offer is this long, starts on this grid, and keeps this much clear of anything real in your calendar.

Notifications
Allow notifications

A notification is how you find out a request is waiting, and it carries Accept and Decline. The person’s name and note appear in it.

This device
Publishes your page✓
Key in your iCloud Keychain✓
Request page

Other devices can answer requests; only this one publishes. The page’s key is in your iCloud Keychain, so a new device or a reinstall finds it. Switching off stops publishing at once.
